mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months reduces expected equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for ≥2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite sustained FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for ≥2 months (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (indicated by negative HOUST) signal weakening labor market strength, which precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns are positive when PAYEMS up and HOUST down, or the pattern reverses in >40% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, coinciding with a decline in consumer demand proxy (HOUST), predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as supply catches up with demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 12-month MA while HOUST falls by ≥5% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the described INDPRO/HOUST pattern in >70% of similar events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the RSAFS (raw material prices) below the 50-week simple moving average, during a rising CPIAUCSL (inflation), predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as cost pressures suppress margins.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 50-week SMA and CPIAUCSL rising in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when RSAFS < 50-SMA and CPIAUCSL rising, or the pattern fails to predict direction in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months indicates labor market softening, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days in a non-recessionary environment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive when UNRATE < 4% for ≥3 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly PAYEMS (employment changes) exceeding 200,000 while GDP-related demand proxies (e.g., GDPC1) remain flat, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as market anticipates over-employment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and GDPC1 flat in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when PAYEMS spikes and GDPC1 flat, or the pattern fails to predict direction in >50% of events.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in both HOUST (housing starts) and INDPRO (industrial output) above their prior month's levels, without a corresponding CPIAUCSL increase, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as broad demand accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST up, INDPRO up, CPIAUCSL flat or down in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the pattern occurs in >60% of similar months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in FEDFUNDS below 1% for two consecutive months in a non-inflationary context predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as rates are expected to stabilize and growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for ≥2 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 0.5% in the same window
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS < 1% for ≥2 months in non-inflationary context (as judged by CPIAUCSL).
